Manuel Rivera

Republican candidate for Attorney General for the District of Columbia · Challenger

Attorney (immigration law)

Manuel Rivera is a Puerto Rico-born attorney in Washington, D.C. who practices immigration law. He announced a run for the Republican nomination for D.C. Attorney General in early 2026 and was unopposed in the June 16, 2026 Republican primary. He faces incumbent Democrat Brian Schwalb in the November 3, 2026 general election.

Where Rivera stands

Juvenile crime
Calls for aggressive action against juvenile crime in D.C. and stronger enforcement of existing juvenile delinquency laws.
Parental accountability
Supports prosecuting parents of repeat juvenile offenders under contributing-to-the-delinquency-of-a-minor laws, and backed reports that interim U.S. Attorney Jeanine Pirro is pursuing such cases.
Puerto Rico status
Has said that one of his goals is to promote independence for Puerto Rico.

Background

  • Attorney in Washington, D.C., practicing immigration law
  • Previously worked as a volunteer lobbyist, according to El Nuevo Día
  • Born in Puerto Rico
  • Republican candidate for D.C. Attorney General, 2026 (unopposed in the June 16 primary)
